breakfast.name: Fatteh (Bread in Yogurt)
instructions: Toast pita, break into pieces
Layer bread, chickpeas
Top with garlicky yogurt-tahini
Brown pine nuts in butter
Pour over, dust with cumin
breakfast.description: Layered bread, chickpeas, and yogurt — a Damascus classic.

breakfast.name: Labneh with Olive Oil
instructions: Spread labneh on plate
Drizzle olive oil
Sprinkle za'atar and mint
breakfast.description: Thick strained yogurt with olive oil and za'atar.

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Omernos~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims).

breakfast.name: Fatteh (Chickpeas with Bread and Yoghurt)
ingredients: Toasted or fried pita bread (broken into pieces)
instructions: Fatteh is the Syrian morning dish of layered chickpeas, bread, and yoghurt
The bread is toasted or fried -- it provides the crunch
Chickpeas are placed on the bread
Yoghurt poured over
Tahini sauce drizzled over
Toasted pine nuts on top -- the garnish
Cumin and paprika as the spice finish
Eaten warm -- the bread softens as the toppings are added
Fatteh is a Damascus specialty
breakfast.description: Syrian Damascus layered breakfast -- toasted pita pieces topped with chickpeas, thick yoghurt, tahini-lemon-garlic sauce, toasted pine nuts, and cumin. Eaten warm; the bread softens as the toppings are added. A Damascus specialty; each layer adds texture and flavor.

breakfast.name: Fuul with Za'atar
ingredients: Za'atar (Syrian herb blend: thyme, sumac, sesame)
instructions: Syrian fuul (fava beans) with za'atar is the Levantine breakfast
Za'atar: the Syrian herb blend -- dried thyme, sumac, sesame, and salt
The beans are dressed simply with olive oil and lemon
Za'atar is sprinkled on or eaten separately with olive oil and bread
Za'atar dipped bread alongside fuul: the Syrian morning combination
breakfast.description: Syrian fava beans with za'atar -- cooked fava beans dressed with olive oil, lemon, and garlic, served alongside za'atar (Syrian herb blend: thyme, sumac, sesame) for dipping bread. The Levantine morning combination.

lunch.name: Kibbeh (Stuffed Meat Croquettes)
ingredients: Filling: ground lamb, pine nuts, onion, allspice, cinnamon
instructions: Process shell mixture until smooth
Make spiced meat-pine nut filling
Shape shell around filling into oval torpedoes
Deep fry until dark golden
lunch.description: Syria's culinary masterpiece — crispy bulgur shell, spiced meat within.

lunch.name: Mahshi (Stuffed Vegetables)
ingredients: Filling: rice, lamb, tomato paste, allspice, cinnamon, mint
instructions: Hollow vegetables
Make filling
Stuff tightly
Pack in pot with sauce
Simmer 60 min

lunch.name: Mulukhiyah (Jute Leaf Soup)
ingredients: Mulukhiyah leaves (jute mallow -- dried or fresh)
instructions: Mulukhiyah is one of the oldest dishes in the world
Eaten in ancient Egypt and across the Levant for millennia
The jute mallow leaves (Corchorus olitorius) -- intensely green
The distinctive texture: mucilaginous, thick, silky
The garlic-coriander fry (takliya) is added to the soup at the end
The takliya sizzles in the soup -- the sound and fragrance are the signature
Served over rice with the chicken that was used for the broth
lunch.description: Syrian ancient jute leaf soup -- mulukhiyah (Corchorus olitorius: eaten since ancient Egypt), jute leaves cooked in chicken broth until thick and silky, finished with a sizzling garlic-coriander takliya. The takliya sound and fragrance are the signature. Served over rice with the boiled chicken.

lunch.name: Shawarma
ingredients: Lamb or chicken (marinated with shawarma spices: cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice)
instructions: Shawarma is the Levantine roasted meat wrap -- the ancestor of the Turkish doner kebab
Meat marinated in warm spices, stacked onto a vertical spit and slow-roasted
The spit rotates continuously -- the outside cooks while the inside stays raw
Sliced thin from the outside as it cooks
Wrapped in flatbread with vegetables and sauces
Syria is one of the birthplaces of shawarma culture
lunch.description: Syrian Levantine spit-roasted meat wrap -- lamb or chicken marinated in shawarma spices (cumin, coriander, cinnamon, allspice), stacked on a vertical rotating spit, outer layer sliced and wrapped in flatbread with tomato, parsley, and toum (garlic sauce). Syria is a birthplace of shawarma culture.

lunch.name: Kibbeh (Bulgur and Lamb)
instructions: Kibbeh is the quintessential Levantine dish -- Syria, Lebanon, Jordan all claim it
Outer shell: bulgur wheat mixed with minced lamb and spices
Inner filling: cooked minced lamb with pine nuts and raisins
The technique: a hollow shell of the bulgur-lamb mixture, filled, sealed, and fried
The raw kibbeh (kibbeh nayyeh): eaten raw like steak tartare -- a Syrian delicacy
Baked kibbeh in a tray (kibbeh bel sanieh): the large baked version
Each Syrian family has its kibbeh technique
lunch.description: Syrian bulgur-lamb croquette -- outer shell of bulgur wheat and minced lamb encasing an inner filling of spiced lamb, pine nuts, and raisins, fried crispy. The raw version (kibbeh nayyeh) is eaten like steak tartare. Syria, Lebanon, and Jordan all claim kibbeh; each Syrian family has its own technique.

dinner.name: Fattoush (Bread Salad)
instructions: Fry pita pieces until crispy
Chop all vegetables and herbs
Make sumac-pomegranate dressing
Toss everything together
dinner.description: Tangy bread salad with sumac and pomegranate.

dinner.name: Shawarma
ingredients: Yogurt marinade: garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, lemon
instructions: Marinate meat in spiced yogurt
Stack on vertical spit or layer in pan
Roast, shave thin slices
Serve in pita with tahini, pickles, tomatoes
dinner.description: Spiced, spit-roasted meat in pita with tahini.

dinner.name: Mansaf (Lamb in Yoghurt Sauce)
instructions: Mansaf is the Jordanian and southern Syrian national dish
The defining element: jameed -- dried, fermented goat milk reconstituted into a sauce
The jameed gives a pungent, tangy, deeply savory flavor
The lamb is poached in the jameed broth
Served on a bed of flatbread layered with rice
Eaten communally from a large platter -- with the right hand only
Mansaf is the dish of celebration, hospitality, and Bedouin heritage
dinner.description: Syrian-Jordanian Bedouin feast dish -- whole lamb poached in jameed (dried fermented goat milk reconstituted into a pungent, tangy sauce), served on a platter of flatbread and rice with pine nuts. Eaten communally with the right hand. The dish of celebration, hospitality, and Bedouin heritage.

dinner.name: Samke Harra (Spiced Baked Fish)
instructions: Samke harra is the Syrian and Lebanese spiced fish dish
The fish is baked or grilled
Covered with a tahini-walnut-chilli sauce
The sauce: tahini, lemon, garlic, coriander, chilli, walnuts
A complex, rich, spiced sauce over the delicate fish
Aleppo pepper (the Syrian mild, fruity chilli) is traditional
dinner.description: Syrian spiced baked fish -- whole fish baked or grilled, covered with a sauce of tahini, walnuts, coriander, Aleppo pepper (the Syrian mild fruity chilli), and lemon. Complex, rich, spiced against the delicate fish.

dinner.name: Maqluba (Upside-Down Rice)
instructions: Maqluba means upside-down in Arabic
The dish is cooked in a pot with the rice on top
Then dramatically flipped onto a platter -- the reveal
The reveal: the layered vegetables and meat appear on top
The rice is on the bottom of the pot but the top of the platter
Eaten in Palestine, Jordan, Syria, and Lebanon
The dramatic flip is the ceremony of maqluba
dinner.description: Syrian Palestinian upside-down rice -- fried eggplant, cauliflower, and potato layered with meat and spiced rice in a pot, then flipped dramatically onto a platter (the reveal). Maqluba means upside-down. The layers appear reversed: vegetables and meat on top, rice below. Shared across the Levant.

snacks.name: Muhammara (Pepper-Walnut Dip)
instructions: Blend all ingredients to thick paste
Drizzle with olive oil
Serve with bread
snacks.description: Aleppo's famous roasted pepper and walnut dip.

snacks.name: Muhammara (Red Pepper Walnut Paste)
instructions: Muhammara is the Syrian red pepper and walnut paste
An Aleppo specialty -- from the great Syrian city of Aleppo
Roasted red peppers ground with walnuts
Pomegranate molasses: the Syrian sour-sweet accent
Aleppo pepper: the mild, fruity, slightly hot Syrian chilli
Eaten as a dip or condiment
snacks.description: Syrian Aleppo red pepper and walnut paste -- roasted peppers blended with ground walnuts, pomegranate molasses (the Syrian sour-sweet), Aleppo pepper (mild, fruity, the Syrian chilli), and cumin. An Aleppo specialty. Eaten as a dip with bread.

snacks.name: Labneh (Strained Yoghurt)
ingredients: Full-fat plain yoghurt (strained through cheesecloth overnight)
instructions: Labneh is the Levantine strained yoghurt -- a cheese made by draining yoghurt
Left to drain for 24-48 hours -- the whey drips out, the solids remain
The result: thick, slightly sour, creamy -- like cream cheese but tangier
Drizzled with olive oil and za'atar
Eaten as a mezze dish or for breakfast
Rolled into balls and stored in olive oil for longer preservation
snacks.description: Syrian strained yoghurt -- full-fat yoghurt drained through cheesecloth for 24-48 hours until thick and creamy, drizzled with olive oil and za'atar. Tangier than cream cheese. Eaten as a mezze or breakfast spread. Rolled in balls and stored in olive oil for preservation.

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Omernos~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims).

snacks.name: Baba Ghanoush
instructions: Baba ghanoush is the Levantine fire-roasted eggplant dip
The eggplant is charred over an open flame
The skin chars and the interior becomes soft and smoky
Peeled, blended with tahini, lemon, and garlic
The smoky flavor from the charring is the defining element
Served with bread as a mezze
snacks.description: Syrian fire-roasted eggplant dip -- whole eggplant charred over open flame until the skin is black and the interior is soft and smoky, blended with tahini, lemon, and garlic. The char is the defining element. Served as mezze with bread.

desserts.name: Baklava (Syrian Style)
ingredients: Sugar syrup with rose water and orange blossom
instructions: Layer buttered filo in pan
Add ground pistachios between layers
Cut diamond shapes
Bake at 175°C until golden
Pour cold syrup over hot baklava
desserts.description: Syrian pistachio baklava — the Levantine original.

desserts.name: Baklawa (Syrian Baklava)
ingredients: Sugar syrup with rosewater and orange blossom water
instructions: Syrian baklawa is the original baklava -- from Damascus, one of the oldest baklava traditions
The Syrian version uses rosewater and orange blossom water in the syrup
The flowers are the Syrian flavor
Filled with pistachios (the Aleppo and Damascus variety)
Paper-thin filo with generous nut filling
The syrup: cool syrup poured over hot baklawa -- or hot over cold
desserts.description: Syrian flower-water baklawa -- paper-thin filo brushed with clarified butter, filled with pistachios, baked, and drenched in rosewater-orange blossom syrup. Damascus is one of the oldest baklava traditions. The rosewater and orange blossom are the Syrian distinction.

desserts.name: Maamoul (Date or Nut Cookies)
ingredients: Semolina and flour dough (with butter, rose water)
Filling: dates (medjool), OR walnuts with sugar and cinnamon, OR pistachios
instructions: Maamoul are the Syrian and Levantine Easter and Eid cookies
Semolina-based dough that is buttery and crumbly
Filled with dates, walnuts, or pistachios
Pressed into wooden molds (talibs) that imprint the pattern
The pattern identifies the filling: different mold = different filling
Made in huge batches before Easter (Syrian Christians) and Eid (Syrian Muslims)
Shared across religious communities -- a unifying Syrian food
desserts.description: Syrian celebration stuffed cookies -- semolina-butter dough pressed into carved wooden molds (talibs that imprint patterns), filled with dates, walnuts, or pistachios, dusted with icing sugar. Made for both Easter (Syrian Christians) and Eid (Syrian Muslims): a unifying Syrian food. The mold pattern identifies the filling.

drinks.name: Jallab
ingredients: Jallab syrup (date, grape molasses, rose water)
instructions: Mix jallab syrup with cold water
Pour over ice
Float pine nuts and raisins on top
drinks.description: Sweet, smoky date-and-rose drink — a Damascus Ramadan staple.

drinks.name: Ayran
instructions: Whisk yogurt with cold water and salt
Serve chilled

drinks.name: Arak (Anise Spirit)
ingredients: Arak (Syrian anise spirit -- distilled from grapes and anise seeds)
instructions: Arak is the Levantine anise spirit -- the ancestor of pastis, ouzo, and raki
Distilled from grapes with anise seeds
Clear in the bottle -- turns white when water is added (the louche effect)
The louche: the oils in the anise become suspended as the alcohol dilutes
Always drunk diluted with water (1:1 to 1:3 arak-to-water)
Syrian arak from the Bekaa Valley grapes
Drunk slowly at the mezze table -- arak accompanies the meal, not just the pre-meal
drinks.description: Syrian anise spirit -- arak, distilled from grapes and anise seeds, turns milky white when water is added (the louche effect: anise oils suspended in dilution). Always diluted 1:1 or 1:3 with water. The Levantine ancestor of ouzo, pastis, and raki. Drunk slowly at the mezze table.
